name: Index By Meaning
description: A card is found by what it means, however the question is worded.
purpose: Helps a person or a run find the card or note they need by meaning, including when they ask in different words.
approach: Embeds each item and ranks stored items by how close their meaning is to the question.
out_of_scope: Looking up an exact identifier or literal string, which needs keyword or content search, and keeping the record of the cards it indexes.
milestones: 1. The labelled card is among the first three results for most questions, and median and tail query latency stay under the interactive caps at a fixed corpus size, measured against a Qdrant server.
knowledge: Embedding only the start of a long item loses facts near its end, an incident pinned by a failing case. Latency of an embedded local store is not the latency of a networked server, and the local embedder is smaller than the deployed one. Multi-tenant isolation by payload filter is preferred over a collection per tenant.
measures_of_success: The labelled card is among the first few results for most questions, mostly paraphrases, and median and tail latency stay under the interactive caps at the stated corpus size.
parameters: Collection prefix, storage path or server url, embedder and vector size, and per-call scope and number of results.
inputs: A query string and optional scope for search; item dictionaries with id, text, payload and fingerprint for upsert and sync.
outputs: Ranked hits with id, score, text and payload for search; counts for sync and count; the number deleted for eviction.
effects: Writes embedded points to the collection and re-embeds only items whose fingerprint changed; never raises, returning empty or zero on error.
usage_notes: Call sync on every run to keep the index fresh, pass a scope so private points stay private, and treat unscoped points as shared. Add a second store by implementing the protocol.

name: Spec Selection
description: The few specification records a request concerns are the ones in view.
purpose: Choose, from an ESOI specification index, the few records a new request concerns and their linked records, so the work starts from the intent that applies.
approach: Select the records an input concerns from a specification index, and return none when no record concerns it.
out_of_scope: Building the specification index, and reading the chosen records in full.
milestones: 1. Labelled requests passed by the gated lexical and vector arm: 76 of 76, with every expected record present and no more than the ceiling returned.
knowledge: The ESOI specification index (version 1 JSON: entries, weighted terms, document frequencies); TF-IDF and reciprocal rank fusion; parallel batched LLM selection as in the card filter.
measures_of_success: On labelled inputs every expected record is selected; a failed vector or model call never removes a candidate; calls equal batches. Standing conditions: The records an input concerns are selected from the whole tree in one model call's latency, with no invented ids and no loss when a call fails.
parameters: k_lexical, k_vector, batch_size, max_workers, expand, model.
inputs: The request text, the loaded index, an optional model provider, an optional vector search callable returning entry ids.
outputs: A SpecSelection: ids best first then linked ids, the candidates shown to the model, which source proposed each, the number of calls and failed batches.
effects: One cheap model call per batch of candidates; none without a provider.
usage_notes: Load the index with load_spec_index (write it with `esoi spec index --out FILE`; its digest says when it is stale), pass the run's provider and the consumer's own vector search over the same entries, then read in full only the returned ids.

name: Search Cards And Specs
description: One search shows the cards and specification records a run concerns.
purpose: Help each run see the cards and specification records it concerns in one ranked set, and see when no solution covers its request yet.
approach: Select a run's cards and specification records from one combined search, labelled by kind and by source.
out_of_scope: Drafting the wording of a new solution, which a run does when this search reports that none covers the request.
milestones: 1. A combined labelled case set exists, with requests whose right answer mixes cards and records, requests with no solution yet, and requests that match only an ideal or a metric. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The merged pipeline scores at or above the recorded spec_selection balanced score and context_selection pass rate on their own cases, and ahead of the two separate pipelines on the mixed cases.
knowledge: How the two pipelines differ today, stage by stage. Candidates: cards from the card repository; records from the ESOI spec index, rebuilt when a record file changes. Lexical: IDF over a card's name, keywords, summary, terms, symbols and content (adapters/context_store_assembly.py), against field-weighted TF-IDF over the index's own terms (core/spec_selection.py). Vector: the card vector store or the Quest backend's search, against an injected local embedder over record lines (core/repo_specs.py). Fusion: weighted reciprocal-rank fusion with keyword above vector (select_context/hybrid_context_assembler.py), against plain reciprocal-rank fusion. Choice: a balanced-tier filter and a consolidation pass (core/card_filter.py), against a confidence gate that calls a model only for an unclear case. Output: a card result carries no kind, a record result does. Wiring: cards are assembled at the start of every run (core/orchestrator_run_begin.py); records only through tools (core/tools_repo_specs.py) or the deep-goal slice (core/spec_slice.py). A mounted store is read in place and never copied; the same principle holds for records. Context a run needs that is not a solution, read against the evolvable-structure skill: ideals decide what better means ("there are one or more ideals defined for every solution, and a practical metric to compare how well each implementation achieves the relevant ideals"), so a run choosing among alternatives or writing a new solution needs them; metrics are how a change is judged ("alternative implementations are compared via metrics"); an intent's vision statement settles which way to go when a request is ambiguous; problems are the entry point when nothing is built yet ("all solutions are motivated by a defined problem"). Reached by link in the working default: a solution brings its ideals, its metrics and its intent's frame; a problem brings its ideals and its intent. Not reached: a request whose words match only an ideal or a metric, when neither the linked problem nor the linked solution matches it; an intent whose folder holds no problem or solution. Folding the names of a solution's ideals and metric into its searchable text, as a card folds in its keywords, is the planned remedy, unmeasured. Tags (esoi/tags.csv) are a cheap filter or boost for the same search, planned and unmeasured.
measures_of_success: On the mixed cases the expected cards and records are in view under one budget; a request with no solution yet returns its problem or intent with "no solution yet"; on each half neither existing metric drops; an assembly makes one model call or none. Standing conditions: Never copy a record into a card store. Label every result with its kind and its source.
parameters: Candidate pool size per source, fusion weights per source and kind, the gate thresholds, which record kinds are ranked directly and which are reached through links, whether tags filter or boost, the shared character budget, and the assembly deadline.
inputs: The task text and run metadata (scope tags, deadline), the card repository and vector store, and the ESOI spec index of the repository root when one is found.
outputs: One assembled context: ranked items, each with its kind (card, or a record kind), source and id, the linked records each brings, a "no solution yet" mark on a problem or intent that no solution serves, the rendered view under one budget, and the sources for the answer's explanation.
effects: Reads cards and records and writes neither; at most one cheap model call, none for a clear or an empty case.
usage_notes: Built: solutions_and_problems_with_links (core/unified_search.py, with adapters/card_views.py for a card store) answers the read-only tool search_cards_and_specs beside find_specs. A run's context is still assembled by the two pipelines side by side (two_pipelines), and what is selected follows the metric: on 2026-10-22 the merged arm led the mixed cases but held neither half against the best free arm on its own cases (spec_selection, context_selection; numbers in the results log), so two_pipelines stays selected. every_record_a_view stays recorded as the alternative and is not built. A "no solution yet" result is the trigger for the run to define a solution, recorded through track-runs-on-records.
